map.title: Open Learning Atlas: Mathematics
map.description: A grade-, course-, curriculum-, and provider-independent map of mathematical knowledge and observable capability.

sources.title: Breadth-first mathematics atlas synthesis
sources.citation: Wilson, Josiah, and OpenAI Codex. Breadth-first mathematics atlas synthesis. 2026-07-21.
sources.notes: Original candidate decomposition developed under the Open Learning Atlas map constitution.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare applied mathematics interfaces
sources.citation: MIT OpenCourseWare. Differential Equations, Materials Mathematics, Game Theory, and Mathematics with Applications in Finance course materials.
sources.coverage_scope: Mathematical structures and methods used across mechanics, physics, biological dynamics, economics, finance, strategic interaction, materials, and scientific modeling.
coverage_gaps: No single course covers all five application territories; domain-specific scientific and empirical review remains necessary.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, figures, code, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Numerical Analysis and Methods
sources.citation: MIT OpenCourseWare. 18.330 Introduction to Numerical Analysis and 18.335J Introduction to Numerical Methods.
sources.coverage_scope: Root finding, interpolation, approximation, integration, differential equations, numerical linear algebra, stability, accuracy, and finite-precision computation.
coverage_gaps: Exact symbolic computation and formal verification require additional specialist coverage.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, figures, code, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.103 Fourier Analysis
sources.citation: Jerison, David. 18.103 Fourier Analysis. MIT OpenCourseWare, Fall 2013.
sources.coverage_scope: Fourier series and integrals, orthonormal bases, Hilbert-space and Lp structure, convergence, transform representations, and probabilistic interfaces.
coverage_gaps: Abstract harmonic analysis, noncommutative analysis, wavelets, distributions, and the full breadth of operator theory require additional specialist sources.
Course sequence is not imported as dependency structure.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose, problems, or hierarchy were imported.

sources.title: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e
sources.citation: Abramson, Jay. Algebra and Trigonometry 2e. OpenStax, 2021.
sources.coverage_scope: Expressions, equations, inequalities, functions, polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, systems, analytic geometry, sequences, probability, and counting.
coverage_gaps: The text's course sequence is not imported, and it does not cover abstract algebra or advanced analysis at territory breadth.
The source audits coverage and terminology; its hierarchy is not treated as a dependency graph.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose or exercise content was imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.06 Linear Algebra
sources.citation: Strang, Gilbert. 18.06SC Linear Algebra. MIT OpenCourseWare, Fall 2011.
sources.coverage_scope: Systems, matrices, vector spaces, bases, orthogonality, least squares, determinants, eigenstructure, positive definiteness, transformations, and SVD.
coverage_gaps: Tensors and advanced numerical linear algebra extend beyond the main course and require specialist supplementation.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, examples, or assessment content was imported.

sources.title: Pre-K–12 GAISE II Report
sources.citation: Bargagliotti, Anna E., et al. Pre-K–12 Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction in Statistics Education II: A Framework for Statistics and Data Science Education. American Statistical Association, 2020.
sources.coverage_scope: Statistical problem-solving process: formulating questions, considering data, analyzing data, and interpreting results with variability throughout.
coverage_gaps: The report is an education framework rather than exhaustive mathematical statistics coverage.
Advanced likelihood, Bayesian, causal, multivariate, and stochastic-process models remain outside this first corridor.
sources.notes: Used for coverage auditing and terminology, not as an imported sequence or source of copied prose.

sources.title: NEOS Guide to Optimization
sources.citation: NEOS Guide. Guide to Optimization. Optimization Technology Center, Argonne National Laboratory and Northwestern University.
sources.coverage_scope: Optimization modeling, variables, objectives, constraints, continuous, discrete, nonlinear, and solver-oriented algorithm classes.
coverage_gaps: Control, inverse problems, simulation, queueing, and decision science require additional specialist sources; solver categories are not dependencies.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, figures, code, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: Book of Proof, Third Edition
sources.citation: Hammack, Richard. Book of Proof. 3rd ed., 2018.
sources.coverage_scope: Introductory proof terrain: sets, symbolic logic, direct proof, contrapositive, contradiction, induction, relations, functions, and cardinality.
coverage_gaps: Coverage is introductory and does not exhaust formal proof theory, automated proving, category-theoretic proof, or field-specific proof methods.
The source is a proof text rather than empirical evidence about learning dependencies.
sources.notes: Used for coverage auditing and terminology, not as an imported sequence or source of copied prose.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook
sources.citation: NIST and SEMATECH. NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods. National Institute of Standards and Technology.
sources.coverage_scope: Scientific and engineering model-building coverage including exploratory analysis, process modeling, fitting, assumptions, diagnostics, comparison, and interpretation.
coverage_gaps: The handbook emphasizes engineering applications and classical methods.
Its software workflow and chapter order are not imported as canonical dependencies.
sources.notes: Used for coverage auditing and terminology, not as an imported sequence or source of copied prose.

sources.title: Mathematics Subject Classification 2020
sources.citation: Mathematical Reviews and zbMATH. Mathematics Subject Classification 2020 (MSC2020). 2020.
sources.notes: Used only as a coverage audit across pure and applied mathematical literature. MSC labels and hierarchy were not imported; MSC is a literature taxonomy, not a learning or dependency graph.
sources.coverage_scope: MSC2020 headings were used to audit breadth across pure and applied mathematical literature and to identify missing or misleading macro territories.
coverage_gaps: MSC2020 classifies mathematical literature rather than observable capability, educational resolution, or learning dependency.
Its hierarchy and labels are not imported as the atlas topology.
Specialist disciplinary and educational sources are still required to review each territory decomposition.

sources.title: The International System of Units, 9th edition
sources.citation: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures. The International System of Units (SI). 9th ed., updated 2026.
sources.coverage_scope: SI quantities, defining constants, base and derived units, unit symbols, prefixes, dimensions, and coherent quantity equations.
coverage_gaps: The SI Brochure is a metrology standard, not a geometry or educational dependency source.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, diagrams, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare analysis courses
sources.citation: MIT OpenCourseWare. 18.100B Real Analysis and 18.125 Measure and Integration.
sources.coverage_scope: Real analysis, proof-based convergence, continuity, differentiation, integration, measure, Lebesgue integration, and function spaces.
coverage_gaps: This source does not exhaust functional analysis; the successor territory also uses a dedicated functional-analysis coverage source.
The source audits coverage and terminology; its hierarchy is not treated as a dependency graph.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose or exercise content was imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.102 Introduction to Functional Analysis
sources.citation: Rodriguez, Casey. 18.102 Introduction to Functional Analysis. MIT OpenCourseWare, Spring 2021.
sources.coverage_scope: Normed and Hilbert spaces, completeness, functionals, duality, bounded and compact operators, Lebesgue measure and integration, Lp spaces, and spectral structure.
coverage_gaps: This course does not exhaust measure theory, nonlinear functional analysis, distributions, Banach algebras, or every operator-theoretic specialization.
Course sequence is not imported as dependency structure.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose, problems, or hierarchy were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare geometry and topology courses
sources.citation: MIT OpenCourseWare. 18.950 Differential Geometry and related topology and geometry materials.
sources.coverage_scope: Rigorous differential geometry with interfaces to topology, curvature, manifolds, and advanced geometric methods.
coverage_gaps: Algebraic, computational, discrete, and convex geometry require additional specialist coverage.
Course order is not imported as dependency structure.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, diagrams, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Mathematics for Computer Science and Theory of Computation
sources.citation: MIT OpenCourseWare. 6.1200J Mathematics for Computer Science and 18.404J Theory of Computation.
sources.coverage_scope: Logic, sets, relations, proofs, discrete structures, algorithms, computability, complexity, reductions, and probability for computer science.
coverage_gaps: Set-theoretic foundations, model theory, category and type theory, and information theory require additional specialist sources.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, figures, code, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement
sources.citation: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology. JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data—Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement.
sources.coverage_scope: Measurand definition, uncertainty components, combination, coverage, reporting, and use of measurement results.
coverage_gaps: The guide does not cover every modern computational uncertainty method or domain-specific conformity rule.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, diagrams, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.703 Modern Algebra
sources.citation: McKernan, James. 18.703 Modern Algebra. MIT OpenCourseWare, Spring 2013.
sources.coverage_scope: Undergraduate groups, rings, fields, substructures, homomorphisms, quotients, and related abstract-algebra methods.
coverage_gaps: General algebra, order, lattices, modules, and advanced categorical interfaces extend beyond the course's coverage.
The source audits coverage and terminology; its hierarchy is not treated as a dependency graph.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose or exercise content was imported.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.04 Complex Variables with Applications
sources.citation: Orloff, Jeremy. 18.04 Complex Variables with Applications. MIT OpenCourseWare, Spring 2018.
sources.coverage_scope: Complex algebra and geometry, analyticity, Cauchy theory, contour integration, series, singularities, residues, conformal mapping, and analytic continuation.
coverage_gaps: Several complex variables, Riemann surfaces, complex geometry, and specialist potential theory require further sources.
Course sequence is not imported as dependency structure.
sources.notes: Coverage source only; no source prose, problems, or hierarchy were imported.

sources.title: Standards for Mathematical Practice
sources.citation: Common Core State Standards Initiative. Standards for Mathematical Practice.
sources.coverage_scope: Problem solving, reasoning, argument, modeling, tools, precision, structure, and repeated reasoning as cross-cutting mathematical practices.
coverage_gaps: The source is a standards document and does not supply territory-level dependency evidence or advanced-mathematics coverage.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, examples, or assessment content was imported.

sources.title: Graph Theory, Sixth Edition
sources.citation: Diestel, Reinhard. Graph Theory. 6th ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 173, Springer, 2025.
sources.coverage_scope: Core finite-graph objects and methods: adjacency, paths, connectivity, trees, matching, planarity, coloring, flows, and advanced interfaces.
coverage_gaps: The source is a disciplinary text rather than an educational dependency study.
This first corridor does not yet decompose matching, planarity, coloring, flow, extremal, random, or infinite graph theory.
sources.notes: Used for coverage auditing and terminology, not as an imported sequence or source of copied prose.

sources.title: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.citation: Illowsky, Barbara, and Susan Dean. Introductory Statistics 2e. OpenStax, 2023.
sources.coverage_scope: Data, descriptive statistics, probability, random variables, sampling distributions, interval estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, chi-square methods, and analysis of variance.
coverage_gaps: The source is introductory and does not exhaust causal, Bayesian, multivariate, stochastic-process, measure-theoretic, or modern computational statistics.
Its instructional order is not imported as a prerequisite graph.
sources.notes: Coverage audit only; no source prose, figures, or exercises were imported.

sources.title: OpenStax Prealgebra 2e
sources.citation: Marecek, Lynn, MaryAnne Anthony-Smith, and Andrea Honeycutt Mathis. Prealgebra 2e. OpenStax, 2020.
sources.coverage_scope: Whole numbers, integers, rational values, ratios, proportions, percent, arithmetic operations, factors, exponents, measurement, basic algebra, and multiple representations.
